extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians and authors preparing manuscripts for submission to Forum of Mathematics (Pi and Sigma)
extracted.subtask_short: submitting to Forum of Mathematics Pi
extracted.subtask_description: Author-facing journal instructions for submitting original research manuscripts to the open-access journals Forum of Mathematics, Pi and Sigma, including scope, submission procedure, peer-review, fees, licensing, and post-publication sharing policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope — Pi as a generalist high-quality journal
rubrics_metrics.description: Pi is the open access alternative to the leading generalist mathematics journals and will be of real interest to a broad cross-section of all mathematicians. Papers published will be of the highest quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong research papers from all parts of pure mathematics and related areas will be welcomed. Aim submissions at work of the highest quality and broad interest across mathematics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope — Sigma as a specialist journal (subject clusters)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sigma is the open access alternative to the leading specialist mathematics journals. Editorial decisions are made by dedicated clusters of editors concentrated in listed areas (Algebra; Algebraic and Complex Geometry; Analysis; Applied Analysis; Computational Mathematics; Differential Equations; Differential Geometry and Geometric Analysis; Discrete Mathematics; Dynamics; Foundations of Mathematics; Mathematical Physics; Number Theory; Probability; Theoretical Computer Science; Topology).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This classification exists to aid the peer review process. Contributions that do not fit neatly within these categories are still welcome. If a paper is rejected from Pi on the grounds that its interest is more specialised, you will be able to submit it to Sigma.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality / prior publication requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of a paper is taken to imply that it has not been previously published and that it is not being considered for publication elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should ensure manuscripts are original and not under consideration at other venues at time of submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission method and account requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts should be submitted via the relevant submission websites (http://cup.msp.org/submit_new.php?jpath=pi and http://cup.msp.org/submit_new.php?jpath=sigma). You will need an account for the submission system, which is separate to your Cambridge Core account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you are unable to submit via the websites, submit as an email attachment to fom@cambridge.org. For login and submission support, visit the submission and support pages; contact the editorial office at fom@cambridge.org for problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review model and editorial decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: All submitted articles will undergo single-blind peer-review. The decision on whether to accept articles will be made solely by the Editors in complete independence from Cambridge University Press.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepted submissions benefit from the full functionality associated with reputable journal publishing (copyediting, typesetting, reference linking, usage statistics, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Services provided to accepted articles
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepted articles benefit from copyediting, typesetting, reference linking, usage statistics, and other modern journal publishing functionality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These services are part of the value proposition of publishing with the Forum of Mathematics journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gold Open Access policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Forum of Mathematics, Pi and Forum of Mathematics, Sigma are both Gold Open Access journals. Articles published in the journal are freely and permanently accessible online under Creative Commons licensing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open Access provides validation, copyediting, presentation, sustainability and functionality in exchange for article processing charges (APCs) paid up-front rather than by subscription.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article Processing Charges (APCs) and payment/waiver policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Gold Open Access publication is supported by an article processing charge (APC), typically paid by the author's funding body or institution. The current rate is listed in the Cambridge Journals APC Price List.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cambridge University Press commits that the APC will be maintained at a rate justified by real publishing costs. Waivers and discounts are provided to authors from low- and middle-income countries based on the Research4Life country list (Group A: waived; Group B: reduced by 50%). Waivers may also be available to those whose funding body and institution do not have funds available for APCs. Payment is handled by Copyright Clearance Centre (Rightslink). No author will be expected to pay out of their own pocket. For more detail about the payment process see the Production FAQ. Any figures provided in colour will be reproduced in colour at no extra cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensing options (Creative Commons)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors can choose to publish under the following Creative Commons licenses: CC-BY (Attribution), CC-BY-NC-SA (Attribution - Non-Commercial - Share Alike), CC-BY-NC-ND (Attribution - Non-Commercial - No Derivatives). CC-BY is the default license but the others are available on request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For information on what each licence allows, see the Creative Commons Licenses page. Users can download, extract, store and index content for the purposes of text and data mining — see the Cambridge Core Terms of Use for more details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sharing and posting the Version of Record
rubrics_metrics.description: When you publish in the Forum of Mathematics journals, you are free to post the final published PDF (the Version of Record) on your own website or elsewhere, in keeping with the Creative Commons license you choose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should ensure any reposting complies with the terms of the selected Creative Commons licence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship with arXiv
rubrics_metrics.description: Pi and Sigma are fully peer-reviewed journals offering modern publishing functionality; as with arXiv, articles will be made freely available to all in perpetuity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journals openly encourage authors to post their submissions to arXiv to maximise dissemination and visibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale and fairness of APCs
rubrics_metrics.description: APCs can be seen as a fairer payment mechanism, provided that the costs on which the charges are based reflect accurately the services offered, and provided that the acceptance process is based on peer review, rather than financial considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open Access APCs relate costs more directly to the means of publication and can preserve aspects of traditional publishing while maximizing dissemination; APCs allow costs to be shared rather than borne solely by libraries via subscription.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact and support information
rubrics_metrics.description: If you experience any problems during the submission process, contact the editorial office at fom@cambridge.org. Submission and support pages provide login and submission support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should use the provided contact channels for submission system issues or when unable to submit via the web form.
